subject: general
question: If the simple interest on a sum of money for two years at 5% per annum is Rs.50, then what is the compound interest when compounding annually at the same rate and for the same time?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of **Simple Interest** for 2 years = 5% + 5% = 10%

Effective rate of **Compound Interest** for 2 years = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = 10.25%

Given, 10% corresponds to ₹50

Value of 10.25% = (50 ÷ 10) × 10.25 = 5 × 10.25 = ₹51.25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹51.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Simple Interest (SI) = ₹50, Time (T) = 2 years, Rate (R) = 5% per annum.

**Formula Used:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 | CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50a75b25eb945fcea9127639a8b2079269471bc4ccc5ed46df8a9a84bc7ed76d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Principal (P) = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (50 × 100) ÷ (5 × 2)

⇒ P = 5000 ÷ 10 = ₹500

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = 500 × [(1 + 5/100)² − 1]

⇒ CI = 500 × [(1.05)² − 1]

⇒ CI = 500 × [1.1025 − 1]

⇒ CI = 500 × 0.1025 = ₹51.25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹51.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference is given by the formula: CI − SI = P(R/100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The difference is given by the formula: CI − SI = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate r% compounded annually for 2 years, the effective rate is r + r + (r²/100)%.
